attributes.decisive_finding: NEW EVIDENCE, stronger than the corpus's existing cross-function bidirectionality. ProcessCritter contains TWO TEXTUALLY IDENTICAL hit-node loops - src/game/enemy/critter.c lines 3331-3340 (base c) and 3378-3387 (base current), same `for (i=0; i<count; i++)`, same `nodeBase = base + i*0x5C`, same body shape. In the TARGET, loop 1 at +0xac emits `li r29,0` + `mr r30,r29` (COPY) while loop 2 at +0x238 emits `li r29,0` + `li r30,0` (REMAT). Our build emits REMAT for both, so we match loop 2 and miss loop 1. Because the two loops are the same source text compiled in the same TU by the same invocation, NO source spelling of the loop initialisation can select the copy form for one and the remat form for the other - any edit applies to both identically. This upgrades the zero-remat family's status for this function from 'empirically dead across ~20 forms' to PROVEN source-unreachable, and is the single named mechanism for cluster (a).

attributes.residual: real 6 = two mechanisms. (a) ONE instruction at +0xb4: target `mr r30,r29`, ours `li r30,0` - PROVEN source-unreachable per the intra-function proof above; WebFrank candidate but requires the dataflow-equivalence audit class that claim.law.live-zero-copy-vs-remat-is-allocator-not-source calls for and that the guard family does not yet carry (it is an opcode substitution with a constant-value side condition, not a recolor). (b) FOUR lines: the gFloorCollisionResult+0x34 address web is r29 in target and r30 in ours at +0x4dc and +0x528. Our-colouring check PASSES: in the target r30 is dead from +0x280 to the end of the function, and in ours r29 is dead across [+0x290, +0x5a0); both streams then reuse r29 identically for the skinChild traversal at +0x5a0. This is a clean disjoint two-web swap and is WEBFRANK-READY under the existing copy_register_fields recolor class. NOT PINNED this session deliberately: a pin freezes the function's source, and closing (b) alone still leaves (a), so the function would not reach EXACT and the pin would only block future work on it.
